title: Fit Matrix Sprint Intro — Suncrest Labs & Redwood
summary: Introductory demo focused on the fit-matrix approach for selecting open models: latency vs. quality tradeoffs, integration points in Redwood API/Console, and Optimize recommendations. Agreed to run a two-week sprint of bench runs and mapping to Suncrest workload profiles.

Customer to provide sample queries and SLO targets
Schedule kickoff for bench sprint (Mon Nov 3)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-29
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Morgan Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Hannah Cho (Redwood Product), Priya Raman (Suncrest ML Eng), Ethan Moore (Suncrest Infra), Dana Park (Suncrest PM), Liam O'Connell (Suncrest CTO)

00:00 Morgan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick us off, um quick agenda — i want to run through the fit matrix approach we use for open models, show how that ties into the console and optimize tooling, and then recommend a bench sprint that maps to your telemetry.
00:18 Priya Raman: yeah thanks, excited. quick note on schedule we are aiming to pick a pilot model by mid-nov so whatever helps speed that up is great.
00:27 Morgan Lee: perfect — i'll hand to diego for a quick console demo then we'll go into the bench plan. diego?
00:33 Diego Alvarez: cool, thanks morgan. uh opening the console now, apologies if the screen share looks a little choppy — low bitrate. so the catalog view — think of it as a candidate pool, we surface performance profiles, quantized variants, kernel compat notes. for suncrest we pre-populated a shortlist based on your latency target of ~80ms p50 for chat-ish queries.
00:55 Ethan Moore: quick Q — are the p50 numbers from your hosted runs or from dedicated infra?
01:01 Diego Alvarez: good call — the numbers shown are from our hosted bench runs on A100-ish profiles, we add a note if a kernel mapping changes on different hardware. so p50 is indicative, we recommend running the sprint on your infra to get exact numbers.
01:15 Dana Park: also curious about cost signals — how do you show cost vs quality on the console?
01:20 Diego Alvarez: great question. in the fit matrix view we plot quality (we use your eval set or our standard bench), latency, and an estimated unit cost per 1k tokens. you can toggle to show quantization impact; the color coding highlights variants that are compatibility risks (e.g., missing fused kernels on older drivers).
01:38 Priya Raman: when you say quality, can we plug our own rubric? we have domain-specific pass/fail for our QA.
01:45 Diego Alvarez: absolutely, that's a big piece — Optimize accepts your eval set and we produce delta metrics and regression alerts. for the sprint i'd ask you to upload a ~2k sample set with ground truth and pass thresholds.
01:56 Liam O'Connell: can you talk about fallbacks — if the short model is cheaper but noisy, can requests automatically fall back to a higher-quality variant on errors?
02:04 Diego Alvarez: yes, routing policies support tiered fallbacks. you can define per-route rules: e.g., try quant-small, if confidence < threshold or latency spikes > SLO, route to quant-medium or full float. we demoed that in our last customer call — it handles both capacity and quality-based routing.
02:21 Morgan Lee: to tie it to the fit matrix — we often recommend a shortlist of 3 variants: a cost-optimized, a balanced, and a gold-standard. the bench sprint helps choose the breakpoint where cost savings are worth the quality delta based on your success criteria.
02:37 Priya Raman: sounds sensible. what about embedding / rerank workflows? are those in the same catalog?
02:43 Diego Alvarez: separate profile, but same catalog. embeddings have different latency/cost envelopes; we show them side-by-side when you filter for rerank pipelines.
02:50 Ethan Moore: back to infra — for the bench runs, will we need to run heavy KV cache scenarios? our workloads are chatty with long contexts.
02:58 Diego Alvarez: yes, for chatty workloads we model KV cache hit rates and simulate the effective latency. the sprint runbook includes a section on sequence length distributions and KV cache priming to reflect your real traffic.
03:10 Dana Park: ok can you walk briefly through the bench plan?
03:13 Diego Alvarez: sure — proposed two-week sprint: week one is model shortlisting and dry-run on a small subset; we do 3-5 models (each with 2-3 quant variants). week two is full bench with your 2k sample, latency stacks (p50/p90/p95), token cost estimates, and quality deltas. we'll produce a fit-matrix CSV and a recommendation doc.
03:33 Priya Raman: will logs show token-level attribution? we need that for cost allocation across routes.
03:39 Diego Alvarez: yeah you'll get token-level traces and trace-linking to calls in the console. we also produce a per-query cost and latency breakdown for the bench.
03:48 Liam O'Connell: security — how do you handle our data for the bench? we can't send PII off-prem.
03:54 Morgan Lee: two options: use redwood-hosted ephemeral bench if data is sanitized, or run the bench internally using Redwood Private agent, we provide a runbook and the bench harness so nothing leaves your VPC.
04:06 Ethan Moore: the VPC-on-prem harness is preferred. can you support our k8s clusters with GPU node pools?
04:12 Diego Alvarez: yes, we support both k8s and direct node images, the bench harness just needs access to GPUs and a small sidecar for metrics. our docs list supported drivers; we'll flag driver mismatches in the compatibility map.
04:24 Dana Park: any gotchas we should be aware of?
04:27 Diego Alvarez: common ones: mismatched CUDA versions causing fused kernel fallbacks (that increases latency), tokenizer differences altering quality numbers, and host memory pressure causing OOM at high concurrency. we'll surface these in the bench report and in the console compatibility notes.
04:40 Priya Raman: about tokenizer differences — is the tokenizer deterministic across your runtimes? we've seen small tokenization drift across libraries.
04:47 Hannah Cho: we try to standardize tokenization in the catalog, but we always recommend shipping a tokenization test vector as part of the sprint. the report will highlight tokenization mismatches and provide a suggested alignment plan.
04:59 Liam O'Connell: what kind of telemetry do you need from us?
05:02 Morgan Lee: ideally: sample queries, target SLOs (p50/p95), typical concurrency, average and max sequence lengths, and any data residency constraints. that will let us prioritize models that map to your constraints.
05:15 Priya Raman: can you also include a rough estimation of engineering effort to integrate the chosen model into our API?
05:20 Morgan Lee: yes we'll include a short integration checklist: client SDK call pattern, fallback routing snippet, and recommended batching/caching settings.
05:28 Ethan Moore: competitor question — one of our vendors, SageAI, claims they can auto-quantize with no perf delta. is that credible?
05:35 Diego Alvarez: in our experience some auto-quant flows work well for certain architectures, but they can mask regressions on domain-specific prompts. the fit matrix helps quantify those deltas; auto-quant can be a starting point but we still recommend domain benching.
05:48 Dana Park: timeline recap — we said pilot model decision mid-nov — what are the dates for the bench sprint?
05:53 Morgan Lee: propose kickoff Nov 3 (Monday), shortlisting Nov 3-4, dry runs Nov 5-7, full bench Nov 10-14, review Nov 17. if that works i'll send invites.
06:04 Priya Raman: that works for us — one ask: can you show the console view of the fit matrix with our own thresholds?
06:10 Diego Alvarez: yes i'll demo a mock with your thresholds — switching screens now. (pause) ok here i toggled your success criteria, you can see some models drop out when we tighten the pass threshold.
06:25 Priya Raman: interesting, the cost-optimized variant looks good on p50 but fails in one of our pass items at 12% error.
06:31 Diego Alvarez: that's the kind of signal we capture in the delta table — it will show per-metric deltas and a suggested fallback rule for that specific failure mode.
06:40 Liam O'Connell: will this be reproducible on our infra? what's the variance between hosted and private runs?
06:45 Diego Alvarez: variance is usually within 10-20% for p90 depending on kernel support and driver versions; we call that out and provide kernel remap suggestions.
06:54 Morgan Lee: ok let's capture the explicit asks and owners — (recap) redwood: bench plan, runbook, and seeded shortlist — suncrest: upload samples, define pass thresholds, provide GPU access method.
07:08 Priya Raman: i'll own the sample upload and pass thresholds. Ethan will own infra access.
07:13 Ethan Moore: yep i'll coordinate, we'll try to have k8s creds and a sandbox cluster by nov 3.
07:18 Diego Alvarez: i'll follow up with the console shortlists and a link to the bench harness repo.
07:22 Morgan Lee: great — any final questions?
07:25 Dana Park: minor — what's the expected cost of the bench if you run hosted? just to set expectations.
07:31 Morgan Lee: for a two-week hosted bench across 5 models with 3 variants each, ballpark $3-5k depending on tokens processed. if you're running on your infra costs are just your infra.
07:43 Priya Raman: ok thanks all, that helps. looking forward to the kickoff.
07:46 Morgan Lee: awesome, i'll send the runbook and invites. thanks everyone.
07:50 meeting end
questions: Can we plug our domain-specific rubric into Optimize?
How do fallbacks work for quantized variants?
What telemetry is required for bench mapping?
